report:
### Conclusion
Yes, honey helps reduce acute cough severity and frequency in children aged **1 year and older**, but it **must never** be given to infants under 12 months.

### Key Findings
* **Symptom Relief:** Systematic reviews, including a Cochrane Review, and randomized clinical trials show that honey reduces nocturnal cough frequency and severity while improving sleep quality for both children and parents. Honey performs significantly better than placebo or no treatment, behaves similarly to dextromethorphan, and may be more effective than diphenhydramine.
* **Pediatric Guidance:** The American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) recommends honey (2 to 5 mL as needed) as a home remedy for coughs from upper respiratory infections in children over 1 year old. It is preferred over standard over-the-counter cough medications, which lack proven efficacy and pose safety risks in young children.
* **Infant Safety Warning:** Honey is strictly prohibited for infants under 12 months of age. Raw or processed honey can contain *Clostridium botulinum* spores, putting infants at risk for infant botulism—a serious condition causing muscle weakness and paralysis.

### Sources
* Cochrane Library: Systematic Review on Honey for Cough: https://www.cochranelibrary.com/cdsr/doi/10.1002/14651858.CD007094.pub5/full
* JAMA Pediatrics Trial: https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamapediatrics/fullarticle/571638
* American Academy of Pediatrics (HealthyChildren.org): https://www.healthychildren.org/English/health-issues/conditions/chest-lungs/Pages/Coughs-and-Colds-Medicines-or-Home-Remedies.aspx
* Cleveland Clinic: Infant Botulism Risk: https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/infant-botulism
